ai.title: Use Gemini Flash for file selection
ai.summary: Refactored file selection logic into `backend/src/find-files/`, replacing the monolithic `request-files-prompt.ts` with modular `check-new-files-necessary.ts` and `request-files-prompt.ts`. Switched the primary file-finding model to Gemini Flash via `promptGemini`, removing DeepSeek and complex warm-cache logic from `main-prompt.ts`. Scope covers backend file discovery and prompt orchestration. `countPerRequest` now scales by cost mode (8/12/14) instead of fixed values.

eli5.text: When you ask for help finding files to work on, the system now uses a different, more cost-effective AI model (Gemini Flash) for the initial file selection step. This is a behind-the-scenes change to make file discovery faster and cheaper, and it affects all requests that involve finding relevant project files. You won't notice a direct difference in behavior, but the system now skips the older model for this specific step and uses simpler logic for deciding how many files to look at based on your pricing tier.

ai.title: Add Claude fallback for Gemini file request failures
ai.summary: The `getRelevantFiles` function in `backend/src/find-files/request-files-prompt.ts` now wraps the `promptGemini` call in a try-catch block. If Gemini fails, the system logs the error and falls back to `promptClaude`, selecting `claudeModels.sonnet` or `claudeModels.haiku` based on the `costMode`. Additionally, the prompt instruction excluding test files was removed, allowing Gemini/Claude to potentially select test files if relevant.

eli5.text: When the AI tries to find relevant files to answer your question and the primary file-reading service fails, it now automatically switches to a backup service (Claude) using one of two cost tiers ("max" uses Sonnet, default uses Haiku) instead of stopping entirely. You'd notice fewer failed file requests on rare occasions when the primary service is unavailable. Additionally, test files are now eligible to be selected if the AI judges them relevant, whereas previously they were explicitly excluded. The change is live today.

ai.title: Extract generateCompactId to common util
ai.summary: Moved createRelaceMessageId logic to shared generateCompactId helper in common/src/util/string.ts. Backend now imports this generic function from common instead of defining it locally in relace-api.ts. Supports optional prefix parameter for flexible ID generation. Refactor improves code reuse without changing ID format or behavior.

eli5.text: The system now creates unique message IDs from a single shared helper instead of each part of the code defining its own ID-generation logic. You wouldn't notice anything different when using the assistant, the IDs still look the same (short strings with a 'cb-' prefix), but the change means there's one consistent way IDs are made instead of duplicated copies sitting in multiple files. Behind the scenes, this makes the code easier to maintain and lets other parts of the system reuse the same ID-making process. It's a behind-the-scenes cleanup with no visible change to how anything works.

ai.title: Remove Spinner from tool handler in client.ts
ai.summary: Removed Spinner.get().start() and Spinner.get().stop() calls within the tool handler execution block in npm-app/src/client.ts. This change eliminates the visual loading indicator during tool processing. Scope limited to npm-app/src/client.ts.

eli5.text: When you asked the assistant to use a tool, a spinning loading icon used to appear on your screen while it worked and then disappear when it was done. That spinner animation has now been removed entirely from that process, so you will no longer see a loading spinner appear or vanish while the assistant handles a tool request. If you looked at the screen right now, you would simply see the assistant jump straight from showing the tool action to showing the result, with no spinning indicator in between. The change only affects the tool-handling flow and does not alter any other parts of how the assistant responds.

ai.title: Add Gemini Vertex AI backend integration
ai.summary: New `backend/src/gemini-vertex-api.ts` implements Vertex AI message transformation and `promptGemini` endpoint, mapping OpenAI-format messages to Vertex AI's `Content`/`Part` structure including image `inlineData`. Adds `@google-cloud/vertexai ^1.9.3` dependency and requires `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID` env var. `backend/knowledge.md` updated with per-provider image format specs and Vertex AI message constraints (system message handling, camelCase generation config).

eli5.text: The assistant can now tap into Google's Gemini models running on Google Cloud as a backup option, so when it needs to pick or read your files it has another route available if the primary one fails. Behind the scenes, your project must supply a Google Cloud project ID for this to work, and the system translates its usual message format into the structure Google's servers expect, including how images are packaged. If you looked, you'd see newer log entries referencing Vertex AI alongside the existing model calls, and the internal notes now list how each provider wants its images and messages shaped.

ai.title: Add Vertex Gemini fallback to file request prompt
ai.summary: File request prompt now tries Vertex AI Gemini first, then regular Gemini, then Claude. Adds `promptVertexGemini` import in `backend/src/find-files/request-files-prompt.ts`. Changes error logging to reflect the new three-step fallback chain.

eli5.text: The file request feature now tries a newer Google model first, then falls back to the regular Google model, and finally uses Claude if both Google options fail. This change affects internal staff who handle file requests and makes the system more resilient by adding an extra backup option. If looking at the process logs, you would notice three attempts instead of two when the initial model fails to respond.

ai.title: Swap Gemini API order in request-files-prompt
ai.summary: Reorders API calls in backend/src/find-files/request-files-prompt.ts. Gemini API now tried first, falling back to Vertex Gemini on failure. This change aims to reduce latency.

eli5.text: When you ask the AI to find relevant files, it first tries talking to Google's Gemini model directly, and only if that fails does it fall back to the Vertex AI version of Gemini. This swap in the order of API calls can shave off a bit of loading time when everything works normally. You won't see a new feature or button, but searches might come back slightly faster during the rare moments both services are up. The change was merged on February 8, 2025, and affects internal backend behavior, not any visible interface.

ai.title: Switch check-new-files to Gemini 2 Flash with GPT-4o fallback
ai.summary: checkNewFilesNecessary now calls promptGemini with models.gemini2flash as primary, falling back to promptOpenAI (gpt4o or gpt4omini by costMode) on error. Replaces direct OpenAI-only path in backend/src/find-files/check-new-files-necessary.ts. request-files-prompt.ts log messages corrected to match actual fallback chain: Gemini -> Vertex Gemini -> Claude Haiku.

eli5.text: When the assistant needs to decide whether to look at new files to answer your question, it now tries a newer, faster model first, and only switches to the older model if the new one fails. So you, behind the scenes, get the benefit of a quicker first attempt with a reliable backup plan stitched in, which should mean less delay in getting a good answer. If you were watching internal logs you'd see different model failure messages appear, but you as a user just experience snappier, more resilient responses.
